basis: Progressive skeletal dysplasia; thoracic restriction causes respiratory insufficiency, reported in 1/2 patients, supporting pulmonary involvement with limited frequency evidence.
Appendiceal-origin mucinous neoplasia with disseminated peritoneal occupation; respiratory insufficiency is occasional (5-29%).
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with profound delay and hypomyelination; occasional low glutamine does not establish a separate metabolic phenotype.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; no extra-auditory disease is established.
Cutaneous fibrosis with common (>30%) fascial involvement and disabling contractures; renal impairment is a predisposing condition, not damage caused by this disease.
Osteosarcoma directly occupies multiple skeletal sites; no extraosseous organ involvement meeting the threshold is established.
Carcinoma originates in exocrine pancreatic ducts; liver metastases directly occupy hepatic tissue in more than 30% over the typical course.
Paroxysmal movement disorder with dystonia in 17/21; abnormal movements do not establish primary skeletal muscle damage.
Tick infestation produces a salivary neurotoxin causing paralysis; neurologic dysfunction and the parasitic mechanism define the condition.
Hereditary episodic ataxia; weakness and abnormal eye movements reflect neurologic dysfunction rather than muscle or ocular tissue disease.
Mitochondrial MNGIE with gut dysfunction 7/7 and leukoencephalopathy 6/7; macular degeneration 3/7. Neurogenic bladder 4/7 reflects neural dysfunction, not direct urinary injury.
Congenital infundibular septal malalignment classified under ventricular septal defects.
Basal cell carcinoma originates in skin; nodulation and ulceration remain cutaneous manifestations.
Chronic fungal infection directly damages skin and subcutis; ocular, pulmonary and skeletal involvement is very rare (1-4%).
Bilateral congenital cataracts and subsequent glaucoma define an ocular syndrome.
Defined here as severe hypothyroidism; edema, constipation and lethargy do not establish additional direct organ damage. Autoimmune causation is not universal.
Congenital coronary artery malformation with an intramyocardial arterial course.
Rod-cone dystrophy classified as a congenital glycosylation disorder; systemic annotations lack frequencies establishing common extraocular damage.
Developmental delay and central/obstructive apnea define the disorder; skeletal malformations affect most, including contractures, scoliosis and talipes. Cleft frequency is unclear.
Named muscle/liver syndrome; dystrophy and cerebellar abnormalities are obligate. Retinal dysplasia occurs in 100%; orofacial clefting (80-99%) omitted at the four-axis cap.
Brain and skin hamartomas define TSC1 disease; renal angiomyolipomas occur in 12/15. Pulmonary lymphangiomyomatosis is below threshold (20/78).
Immunodeficiency with hyperinflammation and lymphoid proliferation; ancestry establishes a lymphoid blood disorder, without evidence for additional organ damage.
Inherited hypertrophy of cardiac muscle; syndromic children do not establish extracardiac involvement across this umbrella.
Warburg micro syndrome combines severe neurodevelopmental impairment, congenital ocular abnormalities and characteristic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
Monogenic diabetes with impaired insulin secretion; diabetic organ complications are separate diseases, and antibody positivity alone does not establish autoimmunity.
